content:
Apple has confirmed a special product announcement event next Tuesday (October 13) called 'Welcome home,' but has not yet revealed whether there will be a keynote video. Here is what we know so far.

Apple has not confirmed plans for a 'Welcome home' keynote, but Mark Gurman says there will be an 'online video launch event.'

Apple has taken a different approach to product announcements this year. The MacBook Neo introduced in March was the first example, holding an in-person journalist 'experience' after rolling out other products via press release over consecutive days.

Apple's 'Welcome home' event on October 13 looks like it will break the mold as well.

Unlike a typical event, Apple has not yet added 'Welcome home' to its Apple Events page, and there is no sign of a livestream on YouTube or the Apple TV app.

That could all change in the days leading up to the event. For now, however, it does not look like there will be a keynote video on October 13.

However, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman has indicated there will be a video launch event. In a separate report, he mentions Apple has another event on October 27, as follows:

According to Gurman — who previously nailed down the October 13 date and a home products theme — Apple will hold an 'online video launch event' next week.

Press will attend an 'Apple Experience' event in New York City starting at 9 a.m. local time that morning. So if there is a launch video, it will most likely go live at that time, well ahead of the usual keynote hour.

We expect at least three new products to be unveiled on Tuesday — you can read more about them in this article.

Do you expect Apple to have a keynote ready for the 'Welcome home' event? Let us know in the comments.
